```{r}
# library
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
```

```{r}
getwd()

# Open Data
# Open the CDC CSV
places_raw <- read_csv(
  list.files("Raw Data", pattern = "^PLACES.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
  col_types = cols(.default = "c")
)

# Open EPA walkability
epa_raw <- st_read("Raw Data/Natl_WI.gdb") |>
  st_drop_geometry()

# Open county boundaries
boundaries <- st_read(
  "Raw Data/cb_2025_us_county_500k/cb_2025_us_county_500k.shp"
)

# Make column names lowercase
names(places_raw) <- tolower(names(places_raw))
names(epa_raw) <- tolower(names(epa_raw))
names(boundaries) <- tolower(names(boundaries))
```

```{r}
# Select county identifiers and health prevalence
places <- places_raw |>
  select(
    county_fips = countyfips,
    county_name = countyname,
    state = stateabbr,
    diabetes_adj = diabetes_adjprev,
    depression_adj = depression_adjprev,
    diabetes_crude = diabetes_crudeprev,
    depression_crude = depression_crudeprev
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with(c("diabetes_", "depression_")), as.numeric)
  ) # Convert prevalence values from text to numbers

# Select county identifiers, walkability, and population weights
walkability <- epa_raw |>
  select(
    statefp,
    countyfp,
    walkability = natwalkind,
    population = totpop
  )

# Select county identifiers, names, and map geometry
boundaries <- boundaries |>
  select(
    county_fips = geoid,
    county_name = name
  )
```

```{r}
# Calculate population-weighted county walkability
# EPA measures walkability at the census block-group level, but diabetes and depression data from CDC PLACES are at the county level
walkability_county <- walkability |>
  mutate(
    county_fips = paste0(
      sprintf("%02d", as.integer(statefp)),
      sprintf("%03d", as.integer(countyfp))
    ),
    walkability = as.numeric(walkability),
    population = as.numeric(population)
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(walkability),
    between(walkability, 1, 20),
    !is.na(population),
    population > 0
  ) |>
  group_by(county_fips) |>
  summarise(
    walkability = weighted.mean(walkability, population),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# Add walkability to the health data; keep all CDC counties
county_data <- places |>
    left_join( # Keep every CDC county, even if walkability is unavailable
        walkability_county,
        by = "county_fips", # Match counties using their five-digit FIPS
        relationship = "one-to-one" # Stop if either table has duplicate county keys
    )

# Attach polygons for mapping
county_map <- boundaries |>
    select(county_fips) |> # Keep the merge key and automatically retain geometry
    inner_join( # Keep only counties present in both boundaries and health data
        county_data,
        by = "county_fips",
        relationship = "one-to-one"
    )

# Check missing values
colSums( # Count missing values in each column
    is.na(county_data)
)
```
